title: Circle Theorems: Angles in Circles
description: Use the IGCSE circle theorems - centre and circumference angles, angles in a semicircle, cyclic quadrilaterals, tangents and the alternate segment theorem - to work out unknown angles in circle diagrams (Cambridge 0580 Extended).

notes.heading: The Parts of a Circle You Must Name
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A chord is a straight line joining two points on the circumference. A tangent touches the circle at exactly one point. An arc is part of the circumference.

🔑 How it works
A sector is the 'pizza slice' bounded by two radii and an arc; a segment is the region between a chord and an arc. Examiners expect this vocabulary to be exact - a line from the centre to the circle is a radius, not a tangent.

💡 Worked Example
If chord AB passes through the centre O then AB is a diameter, the longest chord, and it cuts the circle into two semicircles.

notes.heading: Angle at the Centre is Twice the Angle at the Circumference
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Two angles standing on the same arc - one at the centre O, one at the circumference - satisfy: centre = 2 x circumference.

🔑 How it works
If A and B are on the circle and C is on the major arc AB, then angle ACB is half of angle AOB. When C sits on the MINOR arc AB instead, it stands on the major arc, so you must use the reflex angle at O - that is why such angles come out obtuse.

💡 Worked Example
Angle AOB = 130$^\circ$ with C on the major arc: ACB = 130 / 2 = 65$^\circ$. With C on the minor arc instead: (360 - 130) / 2 = 115$^\circ$.

notes.heading: Angles in the Same Segment are Equal
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Angle ACB = angle ADB whenever C and D lie on the same arc cut off by chord AB.

🔑 How it works
Both angles stand on the same chord and the same arc, and both are half of the same centre angle - so they must equal each other. Look for two triangles sharing base AB with their apexes on the same side of it.

💡 Worked Example
If angle DAC = 42$^\circ$ stands on chord DC, then any other angle standing on DC from the same arc - say angle DBC - is also 42$^\circ$.

notes.heading: Angle in a Semicircle is a Right Angle
notes.body:
📌 Definition
If AB is a diameter and C is any other point on the circle, then angle ACB = 90$^\circ$.

🔑 How it works
The diameter makes a straight angle of 180$^\circ$ at the centre, and the circumference angle halves it. Spotting the diameter therefore gives you a free right angle, and the rest of the triangle follows from the angle sum of 180$^\circ$.

💡 Worked Example
AB is a diameter and angle CAB = 35$^\circ$. Then angle ABC = 180 - 90 - 35 = 55$^\circ$.

notes.heading: Cyclic Quadrilaterals
notes.body:
📌 Definition
A quadrilateral with all four vertices on the circle is cyclic. Its opposite angles sum to 180$^\circ$.

🔑 How it works
In cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, angle A + angle C = 180$^\circ$ and angle B + angle D = 180$^\circ$. When the angles are given algebraically this produces a linear equation immediately.

💡 Worked Example
Angle A = (x + 10)$^\circ$ and angle C = (2x - 40)$^\circ$. Then (x + 10) + (2x - 40) = 180, so 3x = 210 and x = 70.

notes.heading: Tangents: The Two Facts That Do Most of the Work
notes.body:
📌 Definition
(1) A tangent is perpendicular to the radius drawn to the point of contact. (2) The two tangent lengths from the same external point are equal.

🔑 How it works
Fact 1 hands you a 90$^\circ$ the moment a tangent meets the radius (or diameter) at the circle. Fact 2 makes an isosceles triangle between the external point and the two points of contact, so its base angles are equal.

💡 Worked Example
Tangents PA and PB with angle APB = 40$^\circ$. Since PA = PB, triangle PAB is isosceles: angle PAB = (180 - 40) / 2 = 70$^\circ$. And PA = 7 cm gives PB = 7 cm.

notes.heading: The Alternate Segment Theorem
notes.body:
📌 Definition
The angle between a tangent and a chord, measured at the point of contact, equals the angle that the chord subtends in the alternate segment.

🔑 How it works
The tangent at A meets chord AB at some angle. Any point C on the far arc gives angle ACB equal to that tangent-chord angle. The chord cuts the circle into two segments, and you use the one on the opposite side from the marked angle. Examiners like wrapping algebra or a centre-angle step around it.

💡 Worked Example
The tangent at A makes 58$^\circ$ with chord AB and C is on the major arc: angle ACB = 58$^\circ$. If the two angles are given as 3x and x + 40$^\circ$, then 3x = x + 40 gives x = 20.

flashcards.example: Cutting along a chord leaves two segments.

flashcards.definition: Angles standing on the same chord from the same arc are equal.

Opposite angles of a four-point-inside-circle quadrilateral sum to 180$^\circ$.

The tangent-chord angle equals the angle subtended in the alternate segment.
A circumference angle at a point on the minor arc uses the reflex centre angle.

questions.stem: A, B and C are points on a circle with centre O. Angle AOB = 130$^\circ$ and C lies on the major arc AB. Work out angle ACB.
questions.explanation: The angle at the circumference is half the angle at the centre on the same arc: 130 / 2 = 65$^\circ$.

questions.stem: AB is a diameter of a circle and C is a point on the circumference. Angle CAB = 35$^\circ$. Work out angle ABC.
questions.explanation: Angle ACB = 90$^\circ$ (angle in a semicircle), so ABC = 180 - 90 - 35 = 55$^\circ$.

questions.stem: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. Angle DAB = 110$^\circ$. Work out angle BCD.
questions.explanation: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180$^\circ$: BCD = 180 - 110 = 70$^\circ$.

questions.stem: PT is a tangent to a circle with centre O, touching the circle at T, and OT is a radius. Work out angle OTP.
questions.explanation: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, so OTP = 90$^\circ$ whatever else the diagram shows.

questions.stem: From a point P outside a circle, two tangents PA and PB touch the circle at A and B. If PA = 7 cm, what is PB?
questions.explanation: The two tangent lengths from the same external point are equal, so PB = PA = 7 cm.

questions.stem: Points A, B, C and D lie on a circle. Angles DAC and DBC both stand on chord DC, with A and B on the same arc. Angle DAC = 42$^\circ$. Work out angle DBC.
questions.explanation: Angles in the same segment (same chord, same arc) are equal, so DBC = 42$^\circ$.

questions.stem: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral with angle DAB = (x + 10)$^\circ$ and angle BCD = (2x - 40)$^\circ$. Work out the value of x.
questions.explanation: Opposite angles sum to 180$^\circ$: (x + 10) + (2x - 40) = 180, so 3x - 30 = 180 and x = 70.

questions.stem: A, B and C lie on a circle with centre O. OA and OB are radii, angle OAB = 35$^\circ$, and C lies on the major arc AB. Work out angle ACB.
questions.explanation: Triangle OAB is isosceles (radii equal), so AOB = 180 - 35 - 35 = 110$^\circ$; the circumference angle is half of that: 55$^\circ$.

questions.stem: A tangent is drawn at point A on a circle, and AB is a chord. The angle between the tangent and chord AB is 58$^\circ$. C is a point on the major arc AB. Work out angle ACB.
questions.explanation: Alternate segment theorem: the angle in the alternate segment equals the tangent-chord angle, so ACB = 58$^\circ$.

questions.stem: A and B lie on a circle with centre O and the minor angle AOB = 130$^\circ$. C is a point on the MINOR arc AB. Work out angle ACB.
questions.explanation: C on the minor arc stands on the major arc, whose angle at the centre is the reflex 360 - 130 = 230$^\circ$; half of it is 115$^\circ$.

questions.stem: PA and PB are tangents to a circle from the external point P, touching at A and B. Angle APB = 40$^\circ$. Work out angle PAB.
questions.explanation: PA = PB (equal tangent lengths), so triangle PAB is isosceles: PAB = (180 - 40) / 2 = 70$^\circ$.

questions.stem: The tangent at A meets chord AB at an angle of 3x. Angle ACB, where C is on the major arc AB, is (x + 40)$^\circ$. Work out the minor angle AOB at the centre.
questions.explanation: Alternate segment: 3x = x + 40, so x = 20 and ACB = 60$^\circ$. The centre angle on the same arc is twice it: AOB = 120$^\circ$.

questions.stem: AB is a diameter of a circle, and ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. Angle CAB = 25$^\circ$. Work out angle ADC.
questions.explanation: Angle ACB = 90$^\circ$ (angle in a semicircle), so ABC = 180 - 90 - 25 = 65$^\circ$; opposite angles of cyclic quadrilateral ABCD give ADC = 180 - 65 = 115$^\circ$.

questions.stem: A, B and C lie on a circle with centre O. Point C lies on the minor arc AB and angle ACB = 115$^\circ$. Work out the minor angle AOB.
questions.explanation: Angle ACB uses the reflex angle at the centre: reflex AOB = 2 x 115 = 230$^\circ$, so the minor angle is 360 - 230 = 130$^\circ$.

questions.stem: A and B lie on a circle with centre O and angle AOB = 120$^\circ$. The tangent at A meets the line BO produced beyond O at P, so B, O and P lie in that order on a straight line. Work out angle APO.
questions.explanation: Angle AOP = 180 - 120 = 60$^\circ$ (straight line BOP) and angle OAP = 90$^\circ$ (tangent perpendicular to radius), so APO = 180 - 90 - 60 = 30$^\circ$.
